note: Every name carries a signed edge_score on -100..+100. There is no call and no threshold: rank on edge_score and cut wherever you like afterwards, which is what makes the ranking question answerable at every k.

findings.finding: GSA exercised Option Period 6 on SAIC's incumbent USACE RITS task order (PIID 47QFCA21F0001) on 2026-06-05 with $35.4M of incremental funding and kept funding it through 2026-08-10, extending the period of performance on the contract SAIC 'lost' out to 2026-11-27 - seventeen days after GAO denied SAIC's protest of the CASTLE-NET award to Accenture.

SAIC raised its MUFG receivables-factoring facility from $300M to $400M on 2026-08-14, seventeen days before the print, despite Note 9 of the Q1 FY27 10-Q showing it was using only $164M of the old $300M cap and had taken zero net operating-cash-flow benefit from factoring in Q1 (versus +$136M in the year-ago quarter).

On 2026-08-14 SAIC raised its MUFG Master Accounts Receivable Purchase facility from $300M to $400M - the first size increase since March 2020 and only the third time in six years it has filed an 8-K Item 1.01 on this facility - signed two weeks after fiscal Q2 closed on 31 July, so the extra capacity cannot touch the quarter being reported; at the last balance sheet date receivables had risen from $853M to $962M (+12.8%) in one quarter on roughly flat revenue, cash had fallen from $182M to $109M, and only $164M of the $300M cap was in use.

A steam-boiler failure took a downstream unit at Natref (63.64% Sasol) offline on 25-26 August 2026, leaving Sasol able to only partially supply jet fuel to OR Tambo, which Natref normally covers 70-80% of, with the repair and recommissioning programme reported to impair refinery production from around 6 September to 4 October 2026.

A FY26 dividend is arithmetically close to impossible: the dividend trigger is net debt excluding leases sustainably below US$3.0bn, net debt was US$3.8bn at 31 December 2025, and Sasol's own FY26 target is only 'below US$3.7bn', so the company would have to beat its own year-end target by US$700m to pay anything.

Six branded aesthetic centers disappeared from So-Young's reported base in Q1 2026 - it had 49 centers at 2025-12-31, the Q1 table shows 11 centers in the 0-3 month ramp-up phase (avg age 2.1 months, so all opened in Q1), and the reported total at 2026-03-31 is 54, not 60; running the same reconciliation backwards gives 0 exits in Q3 2025 (29 + 10 = 39 reported) and 3 in Q4 2025 (39 + 13 = 52 vs 49 reported), so the attrition is accelerating and no city was dropped, meaning these were closures/mergers inside the existing footprint.
findings.adversary_note: Every input to this claim was published on 2026-05-26 in So-Young's own Q1 release and repeated by the CEO on the public call three months before this print - the 54 total, the 11-centre 0-3 month cohort, and the company's own framing 'a net addition of five centers during the quarter'. The word 'net' is management's, not the analyst's, and it is the same word used for Q4 ('a net addition of 10 centers'). More damagingly, the derivation is arithmetically wrong. The cohort buckets are keyed to OPERATING DURATION, and the footnote says explicitly that periods of temporary closure are excluded from that calculation and that relocated or merged centres inherit the predecessor's start date - so centres do not leave the ramp bucket on a calendar clock. Run the migration properly: mature 17 to 20 (+3 graduating from growth), growth 19 - 3 + X = 23 so X = 7 of the 13 December-cohort centres moved up, leaving 6 still inside the 0-3 bucket, and ramp = 6 carryovers + 5 genuinely new = 11, giving net +5 and a total of 54 with ZERO closures. The average-age datum decides it: 6 carryovers at ~3.1 months plus 5 new at ~0.9 months averages 2.10, matching the reported 2.1 exactly, whereas 11 fresh openings spread across Q1 would average ~1.5 and would require all eleven to be crammed into the first four weeks of January - the inverse of the quarter-end back-loading visible in Q3 (10 centres, avg age 1.0) and Q4 (13 centres, avg age 1.2). The identical model applied to Q3-to-Q4 yields 3 carryovers, 10 new, net +10, reproducing management's stated Q4 figure. The claim's 'accelerating attrition' is the boundary artefact of a company that opens stores in December.

findings.finding: So-Young has fallen on three of its last four earnings prints - 2025-08-15 -22.7%, 2025-11-17 -8.5%, 2026-03-25 +9.6% (fully reversed -11.3% the next session), 2026-05-22 -16.5% - and in every one of those four quarters the release itself said aesthetic treatment revenue 'exceeded the high end of guidance', so beating the guide is not what the stock trades on.
findings.adversary_note: I checked the four moves against the Yahoo daily bars and every one is correct: 2025-08-15 -22.7%, 2025-11-17 -8.45%, 2026-03-25 +9.6% then -11.3%, 2026-05-22 -16.5%. The arithmetic survives. The framing does not. First, the magnitude leg is already exactly in the price: the mean absolute move across those four prints is 14.3% and the baseline's event-implied move is 15.05% on a 91.4% ATM IV, so the option market has priced the precise size of reaction the claim's own history implies. Second, the interpretive leg is a wire headline, not a discovery - Investing.com published 'So-Young shares tumble 12% on wider loss despite revenue beat' on 2026-05-22, which is verbatim the claim's thesis, and the 'exceeded the high end of guidance' language is boilerplate in every quarterly release, indexed on SEC.gov, Morningstar and Barchart. Third, 'automated screens cannot recover the dates' is a statement about this repo's EDGAR item-code pass, not about the market: Investing.com, WallStreetZen and MarketBeat all maintain SY earnings-date and reaction pages, because commercial vendors build FPI calendars from press releases rather than item codes. Fourth, the options argument is inverted - 200 total contracts with a 40%-of-mid ATM spread and a skew the baseline could not compute is an empty book, and 0.11 put/call on 200 contracts is roughly 20 puts against 180 calls, one retail order. You cannot argue the book is too thin to compute skew and simultaneously thick enough to reveal complacent positioning. Finally the directional leg is statistically empty: 3-of-4 down carries a 31% probability under a fair coin, and reclassifying the +9.6% print as a loss using the next session is a post-hoc window change, not a fifth observation.

findings.finding: So-Young ran without a permanent CFO for eight months - Hui Zhao resigned as director and CFO effective 2025-12-31 with CEO Xing Jin taking the seat on an interim basis, the Chief HR Officer resigned effective 2026-02-15, and a replacement CFO was only installed on 2026-08-03, four weeks before this print, by moving a sitting independent director (Nan Shen) off the audit, compensation and nominating committees and handing her finance, HR, legal and compliance together.

Revenue per centre in the 4-12 month 'growth' cohort has fallen 26% across four quarters - RMB6.403m (Q2'25, 14 centres), RMB4.818m (Q3'25, 15), RMB4.682m (Q4'25, 19), RMB4.760m (Q1'26, 23) - so each new vintage ramps to a permanently lower plateau against RMB5-8m of capex per store, and the Q2 2026 guide of RMB307-317m implies per-centre revenue falls again given that the 11 Q1 ramp-up centres alone roll into the growth cohort at +RMB29m.
findings.adversary_note: Every input is a line in So-Young's own quarterly press release, and the headline number is an artefact of a definition change the company itself disclosed. The Q2'25 table is headed 'Phase (The length of time since establishment)' - legal registration - while from Q3'25 it reads 'commencement of actual operations', adds an Average Center Age column, re-dates relocated or merged centres to the predecessor's start (pushing established higher-revenue units up into Maturity), excludes temporarily-closed periods (pushing renovation-disrupted units down into Growth) and drops converted centres entirely. The whole '26% over four quarters' is the single non-comparable step at that break: 6.403 to 4.818 is -24.7%, and the three like-for-like quarters that follow are 4.818, 4.682, 4.760 - flat, with the last UP sequentially, while the cohort's average age rose 6.5 to 7.1 to 8.0 months and membership grew 15 to 19 to 23. The claim's central mechanism, that each new vintage ramps to a permanently lower plateau, is refuted by the same published table: the Maturity cohort, where those vintages land, went 7.271 to 8.384 to 7.500 (the Chinese New Year trough), up 3% versus Q3'25 even while absorbing six graduating vintages and expanding from 14 to 20 centres. The forward leg is weaker still: that the RMB307-317m guide 'implies per-centre revenue falls again' is arithmetic on a figure management published on 2026-05-22, where management stated it expects per-centre revenue to keep climbing. The industry corroboration is the most published part of all - Bloomberg ran the Chinese aesthetics price-war story on 2025-09-21 naming So-Young itself as the price-cutter.

findings.finding: So-Young's clinic network stopped growing in Q2 2026: management stated 54 aesthetic centres in 16 cities as of 2026-03-31 (five added in Q1), and an independent Chinese trade piece written on 2026-06-23 still describes the network as exactly 54 clinics in 16 cities - versus +19 stores in H2 2025 - meaning the company is five stores into a stated 2026 plan of at least 35 new stores at the halfway point.
findings.adversary_note: The claim's central premise is contradicted by the company's own primary disclosure. On the Q1 2026 call (2026-05-22) So-Young stated 59 centres across 17 cities as of the call date, a net +10 versus 49/15 at year-end 2025, meaning five centres were added in Q1 and another five between 2026-03-31 and 2026-05-22 - roughly the same run-rate seven weeks into Q2. The network had not stopped growing when it was last actually counted. The 2026-06-23 ichaoqi piece is therefore not an independent recount: it asserts 54 clinics in 16 cities with no source and no as-of date, reproducing the March-31 quarter-end press-release figure verbatim and undercounting the company's own publicly stated position by five stores and one city a full month later. That is an absence of reporting, not evidence of a freeze - exactly the failure mode this hypothesis needed to clear. Separately, to the extent openings are slowing, management published it itself in the same release: 'while maintaining a measured expansion pace'. Finally the sign is not what the claimant assumes: their own mechanism (new clinics unprofitable for 0-12 months) makes fewer openings accretive to the Q2 loss line.

findings.finding: So-Young's cash consumption collapsed to RMB 56.4m in Q1 2026 (cash, restricted cash, term deposits and short-term investments of RMB 880.0m at 2026-03-31 versus RMB 936.4m at 2025-12-31), against the RMB 300m-plus per quarter burn that the most widely circulated Chinese analysis of the name asserted three months earlier.
findings.adversary_note: The exact figure the claim is built on - RMB880.0m of cash, restricted cash, term deposits and short-term investments at 2026-03-31 versus RMB936.4m at 2025-12-31 - is a verbatim line item in So-Young's own PR Newswire release of 2026-05-22, syndicated the same day to TradingView, Benzinga, TipRanks, Nasdaq and Investing.com. It has been public for one hundred days. Worse for the claim, the deceleration it purports to discover was already published two months earlier: the 2026-03-25 Q4/FY2025 release put the balance at RMB936.4m against RMB942.8m at 2025-09-30, i.e. Q4 2025 cash use of RMB6.4m. Against that series the Q1 2026 figure is not a collapse to a low run-rate, it is a quarter-on-quarter ACCELERATION of burn from 6.4m to 56.4m. The stale RMB300m-plus per quarter figure being refuted is a self-media arithmetic error: Huxiu took the RMB310m nine-month decline from 1,253.2m to 942.8m and captioned it as a single quarter. No wire, no sell-side note and no company document ever carried a 300m quarterly run-rate, so there is no priced belief for this finding to correct. And the market did react to this disclosure: SY traded down about 9.4% premarket on 2026-05-22 with the cash line in front of it. A fact that was published, that moved the price the wrong way, and whose direction the claim has inverted, is priced.

findings.finding: At 2026-03-31, 41 of 54 clinics were profitable (up 15 quarter-on-quarter, three times the number of stores added) and 48 of 54 were operating-cash-flow positive (up 9), with aesthetic treatment services gross margin up 8.4 percentage points year-on-year to 27%; the disclosed cohort table (20 mature at ~RMB 7.5m/quarter, 23 growth at ~RMB 4.8m, 11 ramp-up at ~RMB 2.1m) means cohort maturation alone plausibly covers most of the RMB 307-317m Q2 revenue guidance without any new stores.
findings.adversary_note: The claim's load-bearing premise - that the cohort table exists only in the transcript of a nano-cap ADR call - is factually wrong, verified by fetching the source. Every figure cited is in So-Young's own PR Newswire release of 2026-05-22 and therefore the 6-K: 41 centres profitable, 48 with positive quarterly operating cash flow, plus the full cohort table (11 ramp-up at RMB2.1m, 23 growth at RMB4.8m, 20 mature at RMB7.5m per centre per quarter). It also travelled: guancha.cn and ITBear reproduced the per-stage table verbatim in Chinese, and the transcript was syndicated by Motley Fool, Benzinga, Globe and Mail, Yahoo and AOL. Worse for the claim, the RMB307-317m Q2 guidance sits in that same release and is management's own forecast built off that same cohort plus the 59 centres open at report date - so 'cohort maturation covers most of guidance' is not a discovery, it is the assertion that the company will hit its published guidance, which is the consensus anchor for this print by definition. The market already adjudicated this trade-off once: on 2026-05-22 it had both the store-level profitability data and the widening loss in front of it and chose the loss, taking the stock down ~12% pre-market. Finally the mechanism does not reach the consolidated line: 41 of 54 stores were profitable in the very quarter attributable net loss widened to RMB49.2m from RMB33.1m while the high-margin legacy information-services segment fell 34.0% to RMB80.3m.

findings.finding: On 2026-06-09, fourteen ministries led by the National Health Commission and the healthcare security administration published the 2026 work plan for correcting malpractice in medical services, which for the first time names medical-aesthetics abuses explicitly - unqualified providers, illegal 'light medical aesthetics crash courses', and false commercial marketing - all three of which describe So-Young's rapid-scaling discount clinic chain, which had already been named at the March 2026 CCTV 3.15 gala over exosome listings.

The $3.75m registered direct closes 'on or about August 31, 2026' - the same session as the bmo print - delivering 1,348,921 registered, free-trading ADSs into a stock whose 20-day average volume is 9,660 ADSs, roughly 140 sessions of turnover arriving in one day.
findings.adversary_note: The closing date is not a discovery, it is a sentence in the headline press release the claim itself cites: 'The closing of the offering is expected to occur on or about August 31, 2026' ran on PR Newswire at 08:00 ET on 2026-08-28 and was repeated by Investing.com and StockTitan the same day. The tape then expressed a view: 47,836 ADSs traded on 08-28 against the 9,660 ADV the claim uses as its denominator - 5.0x ADV in one session - and the stock marked -5.80% from $2.76 to $2.60. That breaks the claim's own arithmetic: '140 sessions of turnover' is computed on a base the announcement had already invalidated fivefold, and on the post-news base the deal is roughly 28 sessions. The supply mechanism is also mis-specified. There is no discount: the 2026-08-27 close was $2.76 and the deal priced at $2.78, a 0.7% PREMIUM, which is the Nasdaq 5635(d) Minimum Price structure used precisely because 150% warrant coverage is attached - the buyer's economics sit in a five-year $2.78 warrant that is out of the money at $2.60, so selling the share leg at $2.60 books a 6.5% loss to protect nothing. The warrants are unregistered under Section 4(a)(2), so the exercise-and-dump channel does not exist. And trading below deal price cannot be flowback: the claimant concedes the shares did not yet exist and could not be sold. Finally 'no option chain so no one expressed a view' inverts the evidence - absence of options is not absence of pricing when there is a 5x-ADV cash tape and a -5.8% mark on the day the fact became public.

findings.finding: Management sold ~30% of the ADS base at a discount to the prior tape three days before its own results, with 150% warrant coverage (2,023,382 warrants on 1,348,921 shares) AND repriced 277,273 previously issued warrants down to $2.78 and extended them to 2031 - terms a company expecting a good print on Aug 31 would have waited three days to avoid.
findings.adversary_note: The claim's load-bearing assertion is that wire coverage carried the headline dilution but not the structure. That is false against the tape of record: Investing.com's 2026-08-28 story carries the 2,023,382 warrant ADSs, the $2.78 exercise price, the five-year expiry AND the amendment repricing 277,273 existing ADSs to $2.78 and extending them to 2031-08-31, under its own subheading. Every number in the claim, including the 150% coverage ratio, is arithmetic on figures published in the release and the accompanying 6-K on 2026-08-28. The price then did what a market that had read the structure would do: BLRX closed at $2.60, down 5.80%, on roughly 48,000 shares against a 9,660 average - about five times normal - and closed 6.5% BELOW the $2.78 deal price. A financing whose shares trade below the offering price the day it is announced has been fully marked. Two factual premises also break: the registered-direct leg priced at $2.78 against a $2.76 prior close, a slight PREMIUM, so there was no discount to the prior tape. And the AGM authorised-capital increase, which the claimant concedes was public from 2026-08-18, was covered with the headline 'BioLineRx seeks OK for 100B share authorization' - a 5x increase from 20bn to 100bn ordinary shares, a far larger dilution signal than the $3.75m raise and already in the tape. What remains unpublished is only the inference that raising three days pre-print reveals management does not view the print as a catalyst, and that is weak on its own terms: a company cannot market a deal while holding unreleased results, so pricing on 8/28 and closing on 8/31 is the ordinary way to clear the window. At 0.65x pro-forma cash the market has already taken a dim view - agreement with the finding, not information it supplies.

findings.finding: The ClinicalTrials.gov record for Chemo4METPANC (NCT04543071), the source of the pancreatic interim/futility analysis BioLineRx has guided to 'in 2026', still describes a NON-randomized Simon optimal 2-stage design with 10 estimated patients (expansion to 40) and a June 2028 primary completion, and has not been updated since 2025-06-16 - through the entire period in which the company told investors the protocol was amended to a randomized 108-patient study and that enrolment had accelerated.

LexinFintech grew Q1 2026 originations to RMB57.9bn, +15.9% QoQ and +12.2% YoY, while its 90+ day delinquency rose from 3.1% at end-2025 to 3.5% — it was adding volume in the exact quarter Qifu was cutting its loan balance from RMB126bn to under RMB90bn, so LX's credit provisioning peaks in Q2/Q3 rather than releasing.

Lexin's offline inclusive-financing business — part of the 'ecosystem' segment management said was nearly 50% of Q1 originations — largely halted from mid-2026 as bank funding tightened, and in July 2026 staff at the Wuhan Optics Valley Financial Port office were given a choice of transferring into collections or staying home on local minimum wage.

FinVolution told investors on 2026-08-27 that its China loan volume was down roughly 50% in July, and Qifu said funding costs rose about 25bp across July and August with conditions still not improved after the late-June collapse of loan-facilitation platform Juzi Digital triggered a sector confidence and liquidity shock.
findings.adversary_note: The claim is not a discovery, it is a summary of two press releases. Qfin's 'external funding costs rose about 25 basis points during July and August' is in its GlobeNewswire results release of 2026-08-25, and FinVolution's China volume being 'down around 50% in July' plus a 30bp Q3 funding-cost rise is in its GlobeNewswire release and call of 2026-08-27, transcribed the same day by Investing.com under the headline 'profit rises as China funding tightens', and by Seeking Alpha, the Globe and Mail, Yahoo and Bamboo Works. The claimant's own wording concedes it: FinVolution 'told investors' and Qifu 'said'. Every LX holder reads the two closest comparables' earnings calls, and the tape shows they did - LX fell 11.28% over the five sessions ending 2026-08-28, precisely the window containing XYF (08-24), QFIN (08-25/26) and FINV (08-27), leaving it 2.16% off its 52-week low and 65% down over twelve months against FinVolution's 32%. That dispersion is the market already discriminating between these names and assigning LX the worst outcome, which is exactly what the claimant says it has not done. The wider thesis fares no better: LX's RMB57.9bn originations, +15.9% QoQ, come from LX's own release of 2026-05-25 and have been public for three months, alongside management's guidance that Q2 originations would be flat, and a cross-sectional lender comparison naming Lexin, QFIN, FINV and XYF was published on 2026-07-21. Note also the timing: a July volume collapse and July-August funding costs are Q3 events and cannot be in the June quarter LX reports on 08-31.

findings.finding: The NFRA/PBOC 'one-form' comprehensive financing cost disclosure rule took full effect 1 August 2026 with a hard 24% all-in cap, and it targets exactly LX's 'low headline rate + guarantee fee + service fee' stack; the NFRA had already summoned Fenqile by name on 2026-03-13 as one of five platforms over marketing inducement, opaque fee disclosure and collection practices.

Co-founder Yi Wu sold ADSs in the open market on 2026-07-01, cutting his beneficial ownership to 20,196,118 ordinary shares / 6.1%, disclosed in a 13D/A filed 2026-07-06 — an insider reducing at roughly $1.60 into the sector's funding shock.

findings.finding: CBAK's own proxy for the redomicile states the successor Cayman entity will be 'exempt from filing quarterly reports on Form 10-Q under the Exchange Act with the SEC' and also exempt from Form 8-K, and the redomicile became effective 2026-06-23 — meaning Q2 2026, the quarter the 2026-08-31 calendar row refers to, is the first quarter for which no quarterly report is due at all.

CBAK invariably pre-announces its results date by press release with about six days' notice (e.g. 2026-03-24 release for the 2026-03-30 FY2025 print, 2023-08-02 release for the 2023-08-09 Q2 print), yet its IR newsroom shows releases on 2026-07-14, 08-10, 08-13, 08-20 and 08-25 with no results-date announcement, and its events page lists no earnings call for 31 August or 1 September.

The baseline's own EDGAR pull found zero 8-K item 2.02 filings under the new CIK 0002086841, which is exactly what the FPI exemption from Form 8-K predicts — the earnings-release filing channel the aggregators' cadence was built on no longer exists for this issuer.

findings.finding: FRGT concluded on 2025-09-22 that it again qualifies as a foreign private issuer as of 2025-06-30 and would revert to Form 20-F and Form 6-K; it has filed no quarterly report of any kind since the 10-Q of 2025-08-18, filed no Q1 2026 report at all, and has furnished nothing to EDGAR since 2026-07-15 - so no Q2/H1 2026 report is due or scheduled on 2026-08-31.

The Series C preferred shares FRGT is now funding itself with convert at a price reset off the lowest daily VWAP of the seven trading days before conversion, with a floor set at only 20% of the market price on the day before each tranche is issued - so every new tranche resets the dilution reference lower rather than anchoring it.

FRGT holds a standing right to sell up to $1.0 billion of ordinary shares to a single institutional investor under an equity purchase facility signed 2025-10-28, against a company whose entire market capitalisation is now on the order of $1m to $8m depending on which vendor's share count you use.

FRGT has effected four reverse splits inside twenty-three months - 1-for-25 effective 2024-09-25, 1-for-4 effective 2025-05-27, 1-for-5 effective 2025-12-15 and 1-for-5 effective 2026-05-18, a cumulative 2,500-to-1 - which under Nasdaq Rule 5810(c)(3)(A)(iv) makes it ineligible for any bid-price compliance period today, though the 1-for-25 rolls out of the two-year lookback around 2026-09-25 and drops the cumulative ratio back to 100-to-1.
